messages:
Sam: heads-up — last night's ap-southeast surge exposed autoscaler behavior: it spilled into ephemerals ~03:10 UTC and we saw sustained use above configured reserve.
Maya: saw the alert too. prometheus spikes: `sum(gpu_hours{region="ap-southeast"}) by (hour)` jumped ~35% vs baseline.
Liam: quick numbers from dash: steady_reserve_gpus=120, ephemeral_pool=80, observed_peak=210, sustained_5m_avg=160 around 03:12.
Elena: that means ephemeral used ~30 GPUs earlier than intended. latency p50 from 80->280ms for gen models? any KV cache cold starts noted?
Liam: yes 12% cold-kv misses, token latency tail increased. preemption rate for ephemeral nodes spiked (gke-preemptible) causing requeues.
Sam: propose three changes to test: 1) raise sustained_reserve to 140, 2) tighten burst_headroom_seconds from 600->180, 3) longer scale_up_cooldown to avoid chop. Thoughts?
Elena: +1 but tightening burst window may hurt short promos. we should instead add a fast-path for short-lived bursts via prefix caching.
Maya: cost impact estimate? OpsRunner or infra-bot can calc.
OpsRunner: running quick estimate — raising sustained_reserve +20 GPUs ≈ +22% GPU-hours in ap-southeast during peak. If we reduce ephemeral cap and optimize caching, net +8%.
Sam: can we try a canary in ap-southeast only? small window (2 days) and compare tail-latency and cost.
Liam: I can push config to canary cluster. tentative autoscaler config I'm thinking:
```yaml
min_replicas: 30
sustained_reserve_gpus: 140
ephemeral_pool_gpus: 60
max_ephemeral_percent: 30
scale_up_cooldown_sec: 300
scale_down_cooldown_sec: 900
burst_headroom_sec: 180
ramp_step_percent: 20
```
Maya: looks reasonable. also add metric for 'ephemeral_eviction_rate' and alert if >5% in 10m.
infra-bot: NOTE: deploying canary autoscaler config to cluster `ap-southeast-1-canary` — will create PR #3842 and a rollout window 02:00-04:00 UTC.
Elena: add a comms note to support and SRE oncall; they saw user tickets already.
Sam: runbook update needed: include steps to roll back autoscaler and how to drain ephemeral nodes gracefully. also update cost dashboard with canary tag.
Liam: I'll run short Monte Carlo forecast for next 30 days and produce 50/95/99 percentiles by region. ETA EOD.
Maya: thanks. action items: @Liam config + forecast, @Elena runbook + caching plan, @Sam approve canary window, @OpsRunner cost delta and tagging. :thumbsup:
Sam: agreed — will close after we verify latency tails under 95th percentile and cost delta <15% after caching improvements.
